name: Eaton
hq: Dublin, Ireland (operational HQ: Cleveland, OH, USA)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Eaton is executing the sector's most aggressive M&A conversion of an electrical incumbent into a grid-to-chip AI data-center vendor — roughly $12.5B committed across Fibrebond (prefab modular power, $1.45B, closed April 2025), Ultra PCS ($1.55B, closed January 2026), and Boyd Thermal (liquid cooling, $9.5B at 22.5x forward EBITDA, closed March 2026) — while data-center orders grew 240% year over year in Q1 2026 and the Electrical Global backlog doubled. BACKGROUND: Founded 1911; Dublin-domiciled, Cleveland-operated; ~97,000 employees. FY2025 revenue $27.4B (+10%), adjusted EPS $12.07 (+12%). Five segments today; the Mobility group (Vehicle + eMobility) separates via Reverse Morris Trust by Q1 2027, completing the conversion to an electrical/aerospace pure play. Named an NVIDIA 800 VDC data-center power systems partner; unveiled its 800 VDC reference architecture at the 2025 OCP Summit and the Beam Rubin DSX platform at GTC 2026.
ecosystemRole: We assess Eaton as the incumbent making the most explicit bet that AI data centers will buy delivered power systems rather than components — switchgear, UPS, busway, prefab power enclosures, liquid cooling, and on-site generation sold as one grid-to-chip scope. Basis: the company assembled that scope inorganically within 14 months (Fibrebond, Boyd Thermal, Resilient Power solid-state transformers, a Siemens Energy 500 MW on-site power alliance) and its own framing centers on 'grid-to-chip.' Third-party market data places Eaton top-3-to-5 in data-center power and UPS behind Schneider Electric — the order surge (+240% Q1 2026) reflects content-per-megawatt expansion and multi-year hyperscaler frame agreements more than unit-share capture. For BESS and power-electronics vendors in this file, Eaton is simultaneously a channel (its skids and eHouses consume components), a competitor (xStorage BESS, supercapacitor backup), and the clearest read on how incumbents intend to absorb the 800 VDC transition.

productsAndServices.name: Backup power & UPS (9395X family, EnergyAware, supercapacitors)
productsAndServices.description: Flagship 9395X three-phase data-center UPS: up to 1,700 kVA per unit, 97.5% double-conversion efficiency on silicon-carbide converters, ~30% smaller footprint and cooling load than comparable units. EnergyAware grid-interactive UPS (co-developed with Microsoft) lets data-center UPS fleets sell frequency regulation while protecting load — deployed at Bahnhof in Sweden. XLM supercapacitor modules provide fast-cycle bridge power and are a named element of Eaton's 800 VDC architecture.
productsAndServices.positioning: Top-tier UPS incumbent behind Schneider and alongside Vertiv/ABB/Huawei (top five hold ~40-42% of data-center UPS per MarketsandMarkets). The grid-interactive angle differentiates against pure backup vendors.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and distribution; services attach via remote monitoring and predictive-analytics subscriptions.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 800 VDC-era backup shifts toward supercapacitor fast-cycle bridging plus rack-level DC distribution; Eaton's reference architecture (OCP, October 2025) embeds both.

productsAndServices.name: Power distribution — busway, PDUs, switchgear, transformers
productsAndServices.description: PowerWave 2 and Pow-R-Way III busway spanning 225 A to 6,250 A rated up to 600 Vdc with 85 kA SCCR; floor PDUs up to the 1.25 MVA PowerHub 2; rack PDUs, static transfer switches, and remote power panels; medium-voltage switchgear (new Bellevue, NE plant) and three-phase transformers (third US transformer site in Jonesville, SC, hiring from 2027). The PXQ event-analysis system added market-first detection of subsynchronous oscillations caused by AI GPU load bursting, delivered to the installed base by remote firmware update in September 2025.
productsAndServices.positioning: Core of the Electrical Americas franchise (FY2025 revenue $13.3B at ~30% segment margin). The 600 Vdc busway ratings and AI-burst detection are early adaptations to DC architectures and GPU load dynamics.
productsAndServices.roadmap: US capacity race: >$1B invested in North American electrical manufacturing since 2023 (Nebraska switchgear, South Carolina transformers, Virginia PDU/STS expansion).

productsAndServices.name: Prefab modular power (Fibrebond) & modular data halls (Flexnode)
productsAndServices.description: Fibrebond builds engineered-to-order, pre-integrated modular power enclosures (eHouse-class) with equipment installed and tested off-site. The January 2026 Flexnode collaboration extends this to turnkey prefabricated data halls of 3.5-35 MW supporting rack densities above 1 MW, with ~35% average schedule compression versus stick-build.
productsAndServices.positioning: The delivery-speed play: moves Eaton's competition from component price to installed-megawatt lead time. Schneider and Vertiv sell competing prefab modules, so the edge is manufacturing capacity and scope breadth, not exclusivity.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Engineered-to-order project contracts (reported in Electrical Americas).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Fibrebond anchors the Beam Rubin DSX platform announced at GTC 2026 — Eaton's productized AI-factory buildout aligned to NVIDIA's Vera Rubin DSX reference design.

productsAndServices.name: Liquid cooling (Boyd Thermal)
productsAndServices.description: Boyd Thermal, acquired from Goldman Sachs Asset Management for $9.5B (closed March 12, 2026), brings ~$1.7B of forecast 2026 sales — about $1.5B of it liquid cooling: cold plates, coolant distribution, and thermal systems for AI racks. Reported in Electrical Global; 6,000+ employees.
productsAndServices.positioning: Analyst read (RBC): Eaton went 'all-in' on liquid cooling rather than dipping a toe like other players — at 22.5x forward EBITDA, the price demands execution. Puts Eaton in direct thermal competition with Vertiv (which counter-acquired Strategic Thermal Labs, ThermoKey, BMarko) and Schneider's Motivair.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Accretive to adjusted EPS in year two per company; Q2 2026 Electrical Global growth already carried ~25 points from Boyd.

productsAndServices.name: 800 VDC architecture & NVIDIA platform alignment
productsAndServices.description: July 2025 NVIDIA collaboration covering reference architectures and power management for Kyber rack systems with Rubin Ultra GPUs (1 MW racks and beyond). October 2025 OCP reveal of the 800 VDC reference architecture: supercapacitor fast-cycle backup, ORV3 busbar distribution, DC connectors. March 2026 Beam Rubin DSX platform: end-to-end power plus cooling aligned to NVIDIA's Omniverse DSX blueprint with digital-twin assets, scaling from megawatts to hundreds of megawatts.
productsAndServices.positioning: One of three named NVIDIA 800 VDC 'data center power systems' partners alongside Vertiv and Schneider. The architecture cannibalizes some centralized UPS content — Eaton's hedge is owning the replacement content (supercaps, DC busway, solid-state conversion via Resilient Power).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Reference-design-led selling into hyperscaler and AI-factory programs.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Volume 800 VDC deployments track NVIDIA's Kyber/Rubin Ultra cadence into 2027.

productsAndServices.name: On-site generation & energy storage (Siemens Energy alliance, xStorage)
productsAndServices.description: June 2025 alliance with Siemens Energy: standardized ~500 MW modular on-site power plants for data centers (SGT-800 gas turbines plus battery storage), grid-independent, claiming up to two years faster time-to-market with no diesel backup. xStorage containerized BESS (250-1,000 kWh blocks, building and grid-scale variants) for backup, demand response, and grid-revenue participation.
productsAndServices.positioning: Answers the time-to-power bottleneck inside Eaton's own scope rather than ceding it to turbine OEMs — the alliance packages generation with Eaton's electrical balance of plant.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Alliance project contracts; xStorage via direct and channel.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Positions Eaton to sell the electrical scope of behind-the-fence campuses regardless of which generation vendor wins.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Eaton is converting itself from an electrical-components incumbent into a delivered-power-systems vendor for AI data centers, and that the conversion is inorganic by design. Basis: ~$12.5B across Fibrebond, Ultra PCS, and Boyd Thermal in 14 months, the Flexnode and Siemens Energy alliances, and company framing ('grid-to-chip') that sells scope breadth rather than component price.

(High confidence) We assess the data-center order surge reflects content-per-megawatt expansion and lumpy multi-year hyperscaler frame agreements more than unit-share capture. Basis: the underlying market grows ~7.5% annually while Eaton's DC orders grew 200-240%; third-party share structures (Schneider leads; top-5 stable) are unchanged; rolling-12-month order growth of ~38-42% organic is the cleaner metric.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the 800 VDC transition is net-neutral-to-positive for Eaton only if its replacement content wins. Basis: the architecture shrinks the centralized UPS franchise; Eaton's hedge (supercapacitors, ORV3 busbar, Resilient Power solid-state conversion) is announced but not yet productized as a shipping 800 VDC switchboard — a gap independent analysis notes for all AC-switchboard incumbents.

(Moderate confidence) We assess execution risk is concentrated in 2026-2027: four acquisition integrations plus the Mobility spin-off land simultaneously, and the market already prices Eaton for perfection. Basis: repeated post-earnings selloffs on in-line-or-better prints, the Boyd 22.5x multiple, a widening GAAP/adjusted gap from acquisition amortization, and a Q3 2026 GAAP guide below consensus.

(Moderate confidence) We assess backlog duration is a two-sided exposure. Basis: only ~20% of the 307 GW US data-center pipeline converts near-term (bulk 2028+); the backlog gives multi-year visibility but concentrates sensitivity to any hyperscaler capex pause — the order book would show it first.

metrics.name: Revenue
metrics.result: Q4 revenue $6.24B missed; adjusted EPS $2.83 beat, GAAP EPS $2.45 missed the $2.58 estimate

periods.commentary: Record sales and margins, but the Q4 print set the pattern: adjusted-EPS beats with revenue misses, and a market that sells off on anything short of perfection.

metrics.name: Revenue
metrics.result: Q3 and Q4 revenue both came in slightly under consensus; Q4 adjusted EPS $3.33 exactly matched

metrics.name: Adjusted EPS
metrics.result: Beats of 0.3-2.3% per quarter; electrical backlog ended +29% at $19.6B

periods.commentary: Tariffs drove a Q3 guidance miss (shares fell >7%); data-center orders grew 200% in Q4. Growth was real but the stock repeatedly sold off on good prints — priced for perfection.

metrics.name: Adjusted EPS
metrics.result: FY2026 guidance raised to $13.40-13.60 adjusted EPS, organic growth 11-13%

periods.commentary: The strongest print of the run — but one-third of headline growth was acquired, the Q3 GAAP guide sits below consensus as acquisition amortization widens the GAAP/adjusted gap, and Electrical Global backlog +103% carries the Boyd integration bet.
